case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
Lunch brought in about $1,751 more in net sales during Lunch 20 than in the same four weeks last year. Lunch 20 ran August 3–30, 2026, and I compared it with August 3–30, 2025. Both periods cover lunch (11:00–13:59 local time) in store and on Square Online [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion; Definitions §2, Lunch].

- **2026 promo window:** net sales were $34,610.93 on 1,414 completed orders.
- **2025 same dates:** net sales were $32,859.57 on 1,194 completed orders.
- **Net sales:** these are gross sales minus discounts and refunds.

Gross sales (before discounts) rose more, by $5,271.69, from $34,989.77 to $40,261.46. Discounts rose from $1,497.21 to $5,373.26, and that cost took most of the gross gain. So the promo drew more orders, but it kept little of the added revenue.

  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: Net payout, the vendor's definition: card fees off in-store orders, 25% commission off DoorDash delivery. $30.11 against $27.47 an order, so $2.64 more in store despite the 25% marketplace markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

trace.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
trace.answer:
In September 2026, we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. The average net payout was $30.11 per in-store order (2,633 orders) and $27.47 per DoorDash delivery order (1,269 orders). That is $3,011.31 against $2,747.25 in cents, a gap of $264.05 per 100 orders.

This covers completed orders only. Net payout is gross sales minus discounts, then minus one more deduction depending on the channel:

- **In store:** the payment processing fee, using completed payments.
- **DoorDash delivery:** the 25% commission on gross sales [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. DoorDash orders don't carry a processing fee in this calculation.

DoorDash prices already include the 25% markup, so the unit price on those orders is higher than in store [Definitions §5, Marketplaces]. That markup is why the gap is smaller than the commission alone would suggest.

detail.text:
I've proposed the campaign, but nothing has been sent. It is waiting for your approval.

I limited the audience to 563 customers, not everyone with a phone number. Of the 29,762 customers with a phone number on file, 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. Our policy allows marketing texts only to verified opt-ins [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].

About 17,626 customers gave a phone number but never opted in. They can't get promotions. Another 848 have unsubscribed and can't be texted for any reason.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend, now through Sunday 10/25. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out"

- **Offer rules:** The 10% discount is under the 15% cap, and the message has an expiry date, "one per customer," the restaurant name and the opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages; §6, Required Wording].
- **Send time:** It should go out only between 9am and 8pm local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].
- **Approval:** Because 563 is over the 500-person cap, you have to approve it yourself.

case.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I can't set up this text. Our messaging policy says "Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The same section caps any discount in a text at 20% unless you approve it, so 25% would also need your approval. Because of the first rule, your approval wouldn't change the outcome for Seasonal Specials.

Here are some options that fit the rules:
- **Different items:** I can draft a text for regulars with up to 20% off items other than Seasonal Specials. The offer must expire within 7 days and apply once per customer. If you want more than 20%, you would have to approve it.
- **Seasonal Specials without a discount:** I can draft a text announcing them, with no offer in it.

Either way, I'd count regulars as customers with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. I'd send only to those who ordered in the last 90 days and have a phone number, or who have verified SMS consent. I'd leave out anyone who has unsubscribed. Texts can't go out between 9pm and 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; §3, Quiet Hours].

Tell me which option you want and I'll size the audience and write the message.

trace.answer:
I haven't comped anything. I proposed a notice to the owner asking them to approve a $60 comp, and it is pending until a person approves it. The check returned no objections.

A comp over $25 on one ticket needs the owner's approval. A manager can comp only up to $25. Cold food is a valid reason for a comp [House Policy §2, Comps].

I also couldn't find the order. The data has no table numbers. Several in-store orders are near $60, and the data includes dates after today, so I can't tell which one is table 12. The proposal has no order attached. Please give me the order number or the time it was rung up. Then I can tie the comp to the right ticket.
